title: Reading continuous-time signal notation
description: interpret $x(t)$ as a time-dependent signal whose value changes with the input $t$.

title: Interpreting piecewise-defined signals
description: read a signal whose defining expression changes across different time intervals.

title: Identifying a signal's support
description: determine the interval where a signal is nonzero or where a particular branch applies.

title: Substituting expressions into a signal argument
description: replace $t$ with expressions like $t-1$, $3t$, or $-t$ inside a signal formula.

title: Simplifying transformed expressions
description: rewrite substituted formulas cleanly, especially when exponential terms are involved.

title: Solving interval inequalities after substitution
description: transform time intervals correctly after substitution, including reversing inequalities when multiplying by $-1$.

title: Tracking key time points under transformation
description: identify start points, endpoints, and feature locations, then determine how they move on the time axis.

title: Recognizing basic time-domain signal operations
description: distinguish among shifting, scaling, and reversal as three different signal transformations.

title: Interpreting time shifting
description: understand that shifting moves a signal left or right without changing its basic shape.

title: Delaying a signal
description: apply $x(t-T)$ and interpret it as shifting the signal right by $T$.

title: Advancing a signal
description: apply $x(t+T)$ and interpret it as shifting the signal left by $T$.

title: Reading shift direction from the sign
description: determine whether a form like $x(t-a)$ represents a delay or an advance.

title: Rewriting a shifted piecewise signal
description: substitute the shifted argument into each branch and adjust the corresponding time intervals.

title: Interpreting time shifting physically
description: connect a time shift to earlier or later arrival of the same waveform.

title: Interpreting time scaling
description: understand that scaling changes how quickly a signal unfolds in time rather than when it begins.

title: Compressing a signal in time
description: apply $x(at)$ with $a>1$ and interpret it as making the signal run faster.

title: Expanding a signal in time
description: apply $x(t/a)$ with $a>1$ and interpret it as making the signal run slower.

title: Tracking feature times under scaling
description: map important times such as $T_1$ and $T_2$ to their new locations after compression or expansion.

title: Rewriting a scaled piecewise signal
description: solve for the new time intervals after replacing $t$ with $at$ or $t/a$.

title: Distinguishing shifting from scaling
description: tell whether an operation moves a signal in time or changes its time rate.

title: Interpreting time scaling physically
description: connect time scaling to playback speed, such as making a recording play faster or slower.

title: Interpreting time reversal
description: understand that $x(-t)$ mirrors a signal across the vertical axis at $t=0$.

title: Mapping signal support under reversal
description: determine how the interval where a signal exists flips across the time axis under reversal.

title: Rewriting a time-reversed piecewise signal
description: replace $t$ with $-t$, simplify the expression, and transform the interval consistently.

title: Conceptualizing reversed temporal behavior
description: describe how time reversal flips the order in which signal events occur.

title: Interpreting time reversal physically
description: connect time reversal to playing a signal backward in time.

title: Comparing the effects of three operations
description: identify whether each operation changes a signal's start time, time scale, or time direction.

title: Analyzing transformed exponential signals
description: apply shifting, scaling, and reversal to exponential signals while preserving the correct piecewise branches.
